title: Long Lags and Large Returns: Experimental Evidence from Advertising to Businesses
authors: Michael Thomas; Marcel Goić; Kirthi Kalyanam
eligible_reason: Not a staggered binary adoption design. Geography-based switchback experiment randomizing when display ads are on or off by DMA-month; analysis regresses revenue, orders and web visits on 0-12 lags of advertising spend (continuous cost_lag), OLS and IV (adsOn lags as instruments), free or polynomial lag structures, with bootstrap SEs (analysis.R lines 56-110). Treatment is a continuous exposure that switches on and off repeatedly, not a one-time adoption.
design_notes: Shipped repository (LongLagsSimulation) simulates data from the experiment (simulateDGP.R) and runs the paper's distributed-lag regressions on simulated data (analysis.R with feols/fepois; utilityFunctionsLocal.R). Panel key: DMA x yearmo. Full-text hits for 'staggered' and 'two-way fixed effects' refer to the switchback design discussion.
data_files: LongLagsSimulation/data (simulated via simulateDGP.R; real experimental data not shipped)
software_notes: R (fixest, data.table, future.apply); gslab_make Python build system
